en: Yup, <Italic>real</Italic> dangerous. How 'bout we take care o' ya for the night?
Thanks, but no thanks. Now if you'd just let me go...
What's the rush? Pretty little thing like you should be puttin' her safety first.
Don't worry, we'll look after ya. But we'll be expectin' a lil somethin' somethin' in return.
Just leave me alone already.
Y'deaf or somethin'!?
Huh? Can't ya tell we're busy over here, gramps? Whaddya want?
I want ya to quit botherin' the little missus! Y'oughta be ashamed!
If I wanted advice, I'd be phonin' a hotline! Now scram, old man!
Y'little...
Huh? Who're you, his lameass drinkin' buddy?
Drop yer wallet n' we might just let ya walk. Way cheaper than the hospital bill we're gonna give ya if y'don't.
I wouldn't mind if you were just out trying to pick up girls.
But threatening them? Assaulting my boss? Well, I can't let that slide.
What, y'think ya can take us? C'mon, we'll put ya in stitches!
So, you settled into Nagasugai yet?
Yeah, mostly.
Y'got a problem, ya say so, hear me? Us Hakata folk don't feel right if we're not helpin' someone out.
You've done plenty, taking on an unqualified stranger like me. I couldn't ask for anything more.
Not sure I'd call ya unqualified. I hired ya 'cause I knew you'd be perfect for the job.
I have to ask, Chief. Why did you even approach me in the first place?
Good question there. Mm, suppose I just, went with my gut.
It's hard to explain, but I only hire folks I really take a shine to.
And Suzuki-san, y'seemed like a man I could trust. That's why I asked ya on board.
I didn't make a very good first impression, though.
Heheh. Yeah, ya didn't exactly come off like a saint.
But I been drivin' taxis for over thirty years now. Y'get to be a pretty good judge o' character.
I could tell ya had a good heart.
Wish ya'd start leanin' on me more, too. Guess I'm not the most dependable-lookin' fella, though.
Chief... Thank you for everything. I'm lucky I met you so soon after moving here.
Heheh, you're makin' me blush like a beet. Now c'mon, let's paint this town redder than my face!
Oh, this is the place! Hanamidori. Let's start with some of Hakata's famous mizutaki.
There you are, Suzuki-san!
Sorry I'm late, Chief.
Your payment go through all right?
Gotta say, y'really do have it good, Suzuki-san. Guy my age should have a big ol' family by now, but I don't even have so much as a pet dog.
You're still single, Chief?
Well, somethin' in that neighborhood. Anyway, tonight's my treat, so let's stop livin' in the past and start livin' it up!
Now c'mon. It's time I gave ya a proper taste o' what this town's got to offer!
Thank you, sir.
Okay, okay! I give!
Then get lost. I don't want the police involved any more than you do. Besides, I have somewhere to be.
Aaaaaaugh!
(Things could get messy if someone really did call the cops. Better hurry on over to Ose Bridge and meet the chief.)
(Time to head over and meet the chief.)
Hey, pal. I saw you usin' the ATM in there. Y'mind spottin' me some cash? I'm starvin' here.
Sorry, but it was just a bank transfer. I don't have anything on me.
Pfft, ya think I'm gonna fall for that?
I know you got the goods on you. Now fork 'em over!
Sorry, but I don't have time for this.
Y'think ya can just walk away from me!? Yer gonna get it good, ya stingy prick!
...Fine. Let's get this over with.
(Should be able to use the ATM in here for the transfer.)
It's Suzuki. I went and apologized to Tenjin Transportation.
Good, good. They give ya any trouble?
Not really. I'd say it went pretty okay.
Whew, great to hear. Truth be told, the owner over at Tenjin kinda scares me.
Yeah, y'really did me a solid goin' to handle that yourself.
Well, it was my fault, after all. It's only right that I sort it out.
Cut that humility mumbo jumbo outta here, Suzuki-san. I wasn't about to give ya the axe or anything.
What's done is done. Don't go frettin' over it.
Either way, I won't let it happen again.
Well, then...
Just a swingin' sec there. It's payday, right?
How 'bout we hit the town?
There's something I need to take care of, but I'll be free after that.
Sendin' money off again? Bet ya don't keep even half yer paycheck these days.
Yeah, well...
I don't mean to pry or anythin', but did ya leave family behind when you came here?
Not family in the traditional sense. It's kind of hard to explain.
Fair enough. I won't go gettin' too personal.
I just wanna see you with cash in yer pocket and a smile on yer face.
Thank you for understanding, sir.
C'mon, y'don't have to be so formal with me. Loosen up!
Either way, ain't no better time than payday to hit the bars and blow off some steam!
I'll go on ahead. Meet me at Ose Bridge.
See you there.
(First things first, I have to send that money. Better get to a convenience store.)
(Hmm, no one shows up to apologize empty-handed...)
(Maybe it doesn't matter. I'm sure he'll be forgiving as long as I'm sincere.)
(It's probably best to bring a gift.)
(Okay, time to go apologize. I hope the gift I brought is good enough...)
(All right, here I go.)
(There's bound to be a better option out there than this... I'll take a look around. Wouldn't want to leave a bad impression.)
(Tenjin Transportation. This is the place.)
(Well, I've got a gift, so it's time to head to Tenjin Transportation. I think it's on <Color:7>West Gion Street<Color:Default>.)
(Oops... I spent all my money, and I haven't even got a gift yet.)
(Oh well, I guess I'd better head to Tenjin Transportation anyway.)
(I'd better not show up to apologize empty-handed. Maybe I've got something good on me...)
(If not, I should buy a gift first.)
(I think Tenjin Transportation is on <Color:7>West Gion Street<Color:Default>.)
(I should probably buy a gift first. It wouldn't look good on the company to show up empty-handed.)
(I came here already. Let's go somewhere else.)
(I don't need to use the ATM just yet.)
(There's the ATM. I'd better get that bank transfer done so I can go meet Nakajima-san.)
(I've already sent enough money.)
(I should send some money back to Morning Glory. I'm thinking 10,000 yen at least... I know how much they need it.)
(That won't buy much. I should send at least 10,000 yen.)
(I really wanted to send at least 10,000 yen, but that's not an option right now... Sorry, kids.)
(It looks like the money went through okay. That should do for now.)
(My pay should have come in by now.)
You withdrew all of your pay.
(I'll send Morning Glory 20,000 yen for Ayako's Christmas present.)
(Looks like I have enough to cover it. Should I send that 20,000 right now?)
(Okay, this is for you, Ayako.)
You sent 20,000 yen.
(There. May your new shoes carry you where you want to go in life.)
(Actually, I think it can wait.)
(If I send multiple payments per person, it'll get too confusing. I should send the full amount for each kid.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 10,000 yen for Taichi's Christmas present.)
(Looks like I have enough to cover it. Should I send that 10,000 right now?)
(Okay, this is for you, Taichi.)
You sent 10,000 yen.
(Heh. Knowing him, he'll tear around the house with that mask on.)
(Last up is Ayako.)
(She's the eldest of the kids at Morning Glory.)
(I remember her being pretty quick on her feet. Heh... it was all I could do to keep up with her.)
(Although she's more quiet and academically inclined, she's also very athletic.)
(In junior high, she insisted on helping out at home instead of joining a club.)
(We eventually convinced her to join the track team. I hear she's a long-distance runner now, and quite good, too.)
(She's also caring and committed... but I worry she doesn't put herself first often enough. And she needs to learn to take it easy sometimes.)
(That's right... Her running shoes were practically falling apart.)
(Okay, I'll send her money for new shoes. A good pair probably runs about 20,000 yen.)
(I'll send 20,000 yen for Ayako.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 10,000 yen for Koji's Christmas present.)
(Okay, this is for you, Koji.)
(Catch your dreams and don't let them slip, kid.)
(Okay... That leaves Ayako and Taichi. I'll take care of Taichi first since he's younger.)
(Taichi is still a bit of a rascal, unlike Koji. But he always looks after the younger kids, and deep down, he's very responsible.)
(He loves pro wrestling and said he wanted to be a wrestler one day. But now he's talking about working straight out of junior high...)
(I remember wearing a wrestling mask to cheer him up one time. He's been into wrestlers ever since.)
(Come to think of it, he mentioned wanting a wrestling mask once. You can probably get a replica for around 10,000 yen.)
(Okay, then 10,000 yen for Taichi it is.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 6,000 yen for Mitsuo's Christmas present.)
(Looks like I have enough to cover it. Should I send that 6,000 right now?)
(Okay, this is for you, Mitsuo.)
You sent 6,000 yen.
(If you need advice on what to pick... Hmm, maybe I'd better not.)
(Okay, now there's just the eldest kids⑬Ayako, Taichi, and Koji. I guess I'll start with Koji.)
(Koji's an active kid who's into soccer and baseball. He treats everyone equally and is a great example for everyone else at Morning Glory.)
(I seem to remember him talking about a signature series glove he wanted.)
(I think it cost about 10,000 yen. That's more than I gave the others, but no big deal.)
(I'll send 10,000 yen for Koji.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 6,000 yen for Riona's Christmas present.)
(Okay, this is for you, Riona.)
(Good. I have a feeling she'll be happy about this.)
(All right. Number five is Mitsuo.)
(Mitsuo had a crush on Riona. Heh, I even helped him pick out some clothes to impress her.)
(He's got a big heart, and I bet he'd be good for her. I hope things go well for the two of them.)
(It's probably because of Riona that he's been more fashion-conscious. It'd be good to give him some money for clothes.)
(Last time I only spent about 2,000 yen, but he's grown since then. He'll probably need a bit more.)
(Okay, I'll send 6,000 yen for Mitsuo.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 8,000 yen for Eri's Christmas present.)
(Looks like I have enough to cover it. Should I send that 8,000 right now?)
(Okay, this is for you, Eri.)
You sent 8,000 yen.
(Here's a little friend to keep you company.)
(Okay, that's three. Number four is Riona.)
(Riona's probably the trendiest kid at Morning Glory. She likes fashion and loved to talk about the newest fads in Tokyo.)
(She always wore long sleeves to hide the burns she got as a kid. I wish I could be there for her until she comes to terms with it...)
(She had her eyes on a new pair of shoes at the local shopping district, I think.)
(If I remember right, they were around 6,000 yen.)
(Okay, I'll send 6,000 yen for Riona.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 5,000 yen for Shiro's Christmas present.)
(Looks like I have enough to cover it. Should I send that 5,000 right now?)
(Okay, this is for you, Shiro.)
You sent 5,000 yen.
(That should keep your imagination filled with excitement and wonder.)
(Next up are Mitsuo, Riona, and Eri. They're all the same age.)
(I guess I'll start with Eri.)
(Eri's probably the one at Morning Glory who took not having her parents the hardest.)
(That might be why she tried so hard to fit in with the other kids at school.)
(I think she finally learned that being herself was the best way to make friends. She's a survivor, all right.)
(I think she was into rabbit-themed collectibles. She had her heart set on getting a big rabbit plushie.)
(Those probably cost a lot, but I think 8,000 yen would do the trick.)
(Okay, I'll send 8,000 yen for Eri.)
(I'll send Morning Glory 5,000 yen for Izumi's Christmas present.)
(Okay, first one's for you, Izumi.)
(Hope this brings you some holiday cheer.)
(In order of age, next up is Shiro. He's the same age as Izumi.)
(Unlike the rest of the kids, he never liked playing outside. He was bullied in school for a while as well.)
(But he learned how to stand up for himself, and proved he could hold his own. He was also a big reader.)
(I think I'll give him some money for books. He liked books about space in particular, if I remember right.)
(Something you don't come across often would be best. Maybe an encyclopedia of constellations. They go for around, what, 5,000 yen?)
(Okay, I'll send 5,000 yen for Shiro.)
